card: This pull request updates AutoFile and BufferedFile to capture errno on failing fread, fwrite, and fseek calls, appending the OS error message via SysErrorString to thrown std::ios_base::failure exceptions. Currently, I/O failures throw generic strings that discard the operating system error, leaving callers unable to diagnose causes like disk full or permission denied. The author encountered the issue while reviewing wallet dump improvements in #35492. It includes cross-platform unit tests verifying error propagation.
changed_since_previous: Includes AutoFile::seek and fseek failures in addition to fread/fwrite, adding test coverage for seeking before the start of a file.
evidence: PR description: author observed missing OS error details while reviewing PR #35492, which transitions wallet dumping to AutoFile, leaving callers unable to distinguish causes like disk full or permission errors from generic write failures.
problem: AutoFile and BufferedFile throw static, generic error messages on non-EOF I/O failures, discarding errno. Callers displaying or logging exception messages cannot determine why a file operation failed (such as out-of-space, permissions, or invalid seek).

risk.why: Only modifies exception strings thrown on already-failing file I/O operations in utility stream classes.

summary: Captures errno immediately after failed fread, fwrite, and fseek calls in AutoFile and BufferedFile, appending the formatted OS error string via SysErrorString to thrown std::ios_base::failure exceptions. Adds unit test coverage asserting that genuine I/O failures and invalid seeks propagate the OS error.
